exam_set.title: Practice Set 1
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 9, Practice Set 1

questions.jp: 関係データベースのデータ構造の説明として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Kankei dētabēsu no dēta kōzō no setsumei to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which correctly describes the data structure of a relational database?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 親レコードと子レコードをポインタで結合する。
options.romaji: Oya rekōdo to ko rekōdo o pointa de ketsugō suru.
options.en: Connect parent and child records with pointers.

options.label: イ
options.jp: タグを用いてデータの構造と意味を表す。
options.romaji: Tagu o mochiite dēta no kōzō to imi o arawasu.
options.en: Use tags to express data structure and meaning.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: データと手続を一体化（カプセル化）してもつ。
options.romaji: Dēta to tetsuzuki o ittaika (kapuseruka) shite motsu.
options.en: Combine data and procedures through encapsulation.

options.label: エ
options.jp: データを2次元の表によって表現する。
options.romaji: Dēta o ni-jigen no hyō ni yotte hyōgen suru.
options.en: Represent data using two-dimensional tables.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A relational database organizes facts like spreadsheets: rows are records and columns are attributes.

Technical breakdown:
1. A relation is represented as a table.
2. Each tuple is a row and each attribute is a column.
3. Keys relate rows across tables without application-visible pointers.

Japanese keywords to remember:
関係データベース = kankei dētabēsu = relational database
2次元の表 = ni-jigen no hyō = two-dimensional table
行 = gyō = row
列 = retsu = column

Why the best solution works:
エ states the defining tabular model of a relational database.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Pointer-linked parent and child records describe a hierarchical database.

イ:
Tags expressing structure and meaning describe XML-style data.

ウ:
Encapsulating data and procedures describes an object-oriented database.

Memory trick:
Relational means rows related through tables.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: 関係データベースの主キー制約の条件として、キー値が重複していないことの他に、主キーを構成する列に必要な条件はどれか。
questions.romaji: Kankei dētabēsu no shukī seiyaku no jōken to shite, kī-chi ga chōfuku shite inai koto no hoka ni, shukī o kōsei suru retsu ni hitsuyō na jōken wa dore ka.
questions.en: Besides having no duplicate key values, which condition is required for columns that form a primary key in a relational database?

options.label: ア
options.jp: キー値が空でないこと
options.romaji: Kī-chi ga kara de nai koto
options.en: The key value is not null.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 構成する列が一つであること
options.romaji: Kōsei suru retsu ga hitotsu de aru koto
options.en: It consists of one column.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 表の先頭に定義されている列であること
options.romaji: Hyō no sentō ni teigi sarete iru retsu de aru koto
options.en: It is the first defined column in the table.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 別の表の候補キーとキー値が一致していること
options.romaji: Betsu no hyō no kōho kī to kī-chi ga itchi shite iru koto
options.en: Its key value matches a candidate key in another table.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A primary key must identify every row. A missing value cannot identify a row, so primary-key columns cannot be null.

Technical breakdown:
1. Primary-key values must be unique.
2. Every component is subject to NOT NULL.
3. A key may contain one or multiple columns and can appear anywhere in the table definition.

Japanese keywords to remember:
主キー制約 = shukī seiyaku = primary-key constraint
重複 = chōfuku = duplication
空でない = kara de nai = not null

Why the best solution works:
ア supplies the other essential primary-key rule: no null component values.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
A composite primary key can contain multiple columns.

ウ:
Column order in a table does not determine key status.

エ:
Matching another table's candidate key is a foreign-key relationship.

Memory trick:
Primary key: unique and never null.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: 関係データベースにおいて、外部キーを定義する目的として、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Kankei dētabēsu ni oite, gaibu kī o teigi suru mokuteki to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: What is the appropriate purpose of defining a foreign key in a relational database?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 関係する相互のテーブルにおいて、レコード間の参照一貫性が維持される制約をもたせる。
options.romaji: Kankei suru sōgo no tēburu ni oite, rekōdo-kan no sanshō ikkansei ga iji sareru seiyaku o motaseru.
options.en: Impose a constraint that maintains referential integrity between records in related tables.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 関係する相互のテーブルの格納場所を近くに配置することによって、検索、更新を高速に行う。
options.romaji: Kankei suru sōgo no tēburu no kakunō basho o chikaku ni haichi suru koto ni yotte, kensaku, kōshin o kōsoku ni okonau.
options.en: Speed searches and updates by storing related tables near each other.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 障害によって破壊されたレコードを、テーブル間の相互の関係から可能な限り復旧させる。
options.romaji: Shōgai ni yotte hakai sareta rekōdo o, tēburu-kan no sōgo no kankei kara kanō na kagiri fukkyū saseru.
options.en: Recover damaged records as far as possible from relationships between tables.

options.label: エ
options.jp: レコードの削除、追加の繰返しによる、レコード格納エリアのフラグメンテーションを防止する。
options.romaji: Rekōdo no sakujo, tsuika no kurikaeshi ni yoru, rekōdo kakunō eria no furagumentēshon o bōshi suru.
options.en: Prevent fragmentation caused by repeated record deletion and insertion.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A foreign key prevents a child record from pointing to a parent that does not exist.

Technical breakdown:
1. A foreign key references a candidate or primary key in another relation.
2. Insert and update checks reject invalid references.
3. Delete rules preserve the chosen referential-integrity policy.

Japanese keywords to remember:
外部キー = gaibu kī = foreign key
参照一貫性 = sanshō ikkansei = referential integrity
制約 = seiyaku = constraint

Why the best solution works:
ア describes the exact integrity guarantee supplied by a foreign-key constraint.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Physical placement and performance tuning are not foreign-key purposes.

ウ:
Backup and recovery mechanisms restore damaged data.

エ:
Storage reorganization handles fragmentation.

Memory trick:
Foreign key: every reference must have a home.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: E-R図に関する記述のうち、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: E-R zu ni kansuru kijutsu no uchi, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement about an E-R diagram is correct?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 関係データベースの表として実装することを前提に表現する。
options.romaji: Kankei dētabēsu no hyō to shite jissō suru koto o zentei ni hyōgen suru.
options.en: It is expressed on the assumption that it will be implemented as relational tables.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 管理の対象をエンティティ及びエンティティ間のリレーションシップとして表現する。
options.romaji: Kanri no taishō o entiti oyobi entiti-kan no rirēshonshippu to shite hyōgen suru.
options.en: It represents managed objects as entities and relationships between entities.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: データの生成から消滅に至るデータ操作を表現する。
options.romaji: Dēta no seisei kara shōmetsu ni itaru dēta sōsa o hyōgen suru.
options.en: It represents data operations from creation through deletion.

options.label: エ
options.jp: リレーションシップは、業務上の手順を表現する。
options.romaji: Rirēshonshippu wa, gyōmujō no tejun o hyōgen suru.
options.en: Relationships represent business procedures.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
An E-R diagram names the things a system manages and draws how those things are related.

Technical breakdown:
1. E means entity, a managed object or concept.
2. R means relationship, an association among entities.
3. The conceptual model is independent of a particular physical implementation.

Japanese keywords to remember:
エンティティ = entiti = entity
リレーションシップ = rirēshonshippu = relationship
管理の対象 = kanri no taishō = managed object

Why the best solution works:
イ states the two fundamental constructs of the E-R model.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
An E-R model is conceptual and is not restricted to relational-table implementation.

ウ:
Data lifecycle operations belong to process or data-flow modeling.

エ:
A relationship represents an association, not a procedure sequence.

Memory trick:
E-R = entities and their relationships.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 6行だけから成る“配送”表において成立している関数従属はどれか。ここで、X→Yは、XはYを関数的に決定することを表す。
questions.romaji: Roku-gyō dake kara naru 'haisō' hyō ni oite seiritsu shite iru kansū jūzoku wa dore ka. Koko de, X kara Y wa, X wa Y o kansūteki ni kettei suru koto o arawasu.
questions.en: Which functional dependency holds in the six-row Delivery table? Here, X→Y means that X functionally determines Y.

options.label: ア
options.jp: 配送先→部品ID
options.romaji: Haisōsaki kara buhin ID
options.en: Destination → Part ID

options.label: イ
options.jp: 配送日→部品ID
options.romaji: Haisōbi kara buhin ID
options.en: Delivery date → Part ID

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 部署ID→部品ID
options.romaji: Busho ID kara buhin ID
options.en: Department ID → Part ID

options.label: エ
options.jp: 部署名→配送先
options.romaji: Busho-mei kara haisōsaki
options.en: Department name → Destination

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A dependency X→Y holds when every repeated X always has the same Y. In the table, each destination always has one part ID.

Technical breakdown:
1. Compare rows sharing each proposed determinant.
2. 秋田事業所 always maps to 1342, 名古屋工場 to 2346, and 川崎事業所 to 1342.
3. Therefore 配送先→部品ID holds in all six rows.
4. Counterexamples invalidate the other choices.

Japanese keywords to remember:
関数従属 = kansū jūzoku = functional dependency
配送先 = haisōsaki = destination
部品ID = buhin ID = part ID

Why the best solution works:
ア has no pair of equal destinations with different part IDs.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
2016-08-30 maps to part IDs 2346 and 1342.

ウ:
Department ID 500 maps to part IDs 2346 and 1342.

エ:
研究開発部 maps to 名古屋工場 and 川崎事業所.

Memory trick:
Same left side must always mean same right side.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: “従業員”表を第3正規形にしたものはどれか。ここで、下線部は主キーを表す。従業員（従業員番号、従業員氏名、{技能コード、技能名、技能経験年数}）
questions.romaji: 'Jūgyōin' hyō o dai-san seikikei ni shita mono wa dore ka. Koko de, kasenbu wa shukī o arawasu. Jūgyōin (jūgyōin bangō, jūgyōin shimei, {ginō kōdo, ginō-mei, ginō keiken nensū}).
questions.en: Which decomposition puts the Employee table into third normal form? Underlined fields are primary keys. Employee (employee number, employee name, {skill code, skill name, years of skill experience}).

options.label: ア
options.jp: 従業員（従業員番号、従業員氏名）と技能（技能コード、技能名、技能経験年数）に分割する。
options.romaji: Jūgyōin (jūgyōin bangō, jūgyōin shimei) to ginō (ginō kōdo, ginō-mei, ginō keiken nensū) ni bunkatsu suru.
options.en: Split into Employee(employee number, employee name) and Skill(skill code, skill name, years of skill experience).

options.label: イ
options.jp: 従業員技能（従業員番号、従業員氏名、技能コード、技能経験年数）と技能（技能コード、技能名）に分割する。
options.romaji: Jūgyōin ginō (jūgyōin bangō, jūgyōin shimei, ginō kōdo, ginō keiken nensū) to ginō (ginō kōdo, ginō-mei) ni bunkatsu suru.
options.en: Split into EmployeeSkill(employee number, employee name, skill code, years of skill experience) and Skill(skill code, skill name).

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 従業員技能（従業員番号、技能コード、技能経験年数）、従業員（従業員番号、従業員氏名）、技能（技能コード、技能名）に分割する。
options.romaji: Jūgyōin ginō (jūgyōin bangō, ginō kōdo, ginō keiken nensū), jūgyōin (jūgyōin bangō, jūgyōin shimei), ginō (ginō kōdo, ginō-mei) ni bunkatsu suru.
options.en: Split into EmployeeSkill(employee number, skill code, years of skill experience), Employee(employee number, employee name), and Skill(skill code, skill name).

options.label: エ
options.jp: 従業員技能（従業員番号、技能コード）、従業員（従業員番号、従業員氏名、技能経験年数）、技能（技能コード、技能名）に分割する。
options.romaji: Jūgyōin ginō (jūgyōin bangō, ginō kōdo), jūgyōin (jūgyōin bangō, jūgyōin shimei, ginō keiken nensū), ginō (ginō kōdo, ginō-mei) ni bunkatsu suru.
options.en: Split into EmployeeSkill(employee number, skill code), Employee(employee number, employee name, years of skill experience), and Skill(skill code, skill name).

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Employee facts belong with employees, skill names belong with skills, and experience belongs to the employee-skill pairing.

Technical breakdown:
1. Employee number determines employee name.
2. Skill code determines skill name.
3. The pair (employee number, skill code) determines years of experience.
4. Separating those dependencies removes repeating groups, partial dependencies, and transitive redundancy.

Japanese keywords to remember:
第3正規形 = dai-san seikikei = third normal form
主キー = shukī = primary key
技能経験年数 = ginō keiken nensū = years of skill experience

Why the best solution works:
ウ places each fact in the relation whose key fully determines it.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
It loses which employee has which skill and wrongly treats experience as a skill-only fact.

イ:
Employee name depends only on employee number, part of the composite key, so redundancy remains.

エ:
Experience depends on both employee and skill, not on employee alone.

Memory trick:
Put each fact with the whole key that owns it.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: UMLを用いて表した図のデータモデルの多重度の説明のうち、適切なものはどれか。図では、組織側の多重度が1、社員側の多重度が1..*である。
questions.romaji: UML o mochiite arawashita zu no dēta moderu no tajūdo no setsumei no uchi, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka. Zu de wa, soshiki-gawa no tajūdo ga ichi, shain-gawa no tajūdo ga ichi kara tasū de aru.
questions.en: Which statement correctly explains the multiplicities in the UML data model? The diagram shows multiplicity 1 at the Organization end and 1..* at the Employee end.

options.label: ア
options.jp: 社員が1人も所属しない組織は存在しない。
options.romaji: Shain ga hitori mo shozoku shinai soshiki wa sonzai shinai.
options.en: No organization exists without at least one employee.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 社員は必ずしも組織に所属しなくてもよい。
options.romaji: Shain wa kanarazushimo soshiki ni shozoku shinakute mo yoi.
options.en: An employee need not belong to an organization.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 社員は複数の組織に所属することができる。
options.romaji: Shain wa fukusū no soshiki ni shozoku suru koto ga dekiru.
options.en: An employee can belong to multiple organizations.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 一つの組織に複数の社員は所属できない。
options.romaji: Hitotsu no soshiki ni fukusū no shain wa shozoku dekinai.
options.en: Multiple employees cannot belong to one organization.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
The labels say each employee belongs to exactly one organization, while each organization has one or more employees.

Technical breakdown:
1. Multiplicity written near an end counts instances at that end for one instance at the opposite end.
2. 1 near Organization means one organization per employee.
3. 1..* near Employee means at least one employee per organization, with no fixed upper limit.

Japanese keywords to remember:
多重度 = tajūdo = multiplicity
組織 = soshiki = organization
社員 = shain = employee
所属 = shozoku = affiliation

Why the best solution works:
ア follows the minimum of one employee specified by 1..*.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Multiplicity 1 at Organization requires every employee to have exactly one organization.

ウ:
The same multiplicity prevents an employee from belonging to multiple organizations.

エ:
1..* explicitly permits multiple employees in one organization.

Memory trick:
1..* means one or many, never zero.

Correct answer: ア
